topic_contract.scope_statement: Human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and Ebola virus disease; Reston and Bombali viruses are comparison/background entities unless human disease evidence is explicit. Biologically related animal, taxonomic, model, differential-diagnosis and comparative entities are supplementary-only unless material target-specific evidence is also present; only explicit lexical or unrelated hard exclusions are terminal.

related_entity_policy.primary_rule: A related entity alone never establishes the primary target identity.
related_entity_policy.comparison_rule: When target and related entities both have material evidence, retain for primary comparative review.
related_entity_policy.supplementary_rule: When only a recognized related entity is established, retain verified metadata or source-qualified news in the supplementary catalog.
related_entity_policy.hard_reject_rule: Only lexical noise, unrelated homonyms, navigation material, or explicit identifier conflicts are terminal rejects.

authoritative_evidence.name: ICTV Virus Taxonomy Profile
authoritative_evidence.evidence_statement: ICTV separates orthoebolavirus species and distinguishes Ebola, Sudan, Bundibugyo and Taï Forest viruses from Reston and Bombali viruses.
authoritative_evidence.evidence_locator: ICTV online report chapter/genus or family page

authoritative_evidence.name: ViralZone Filoviridae
authoritative_evidence.evidence_statement: ViralZone provides a curated molecular and taxonomic overview used to cross-check accepted names, genome context and related viruses.

authoritative_evidence.name: WHO Ebola Disease
authoritative_evidence.evidence_statement: The public-health source defines the human disease and surveillance scope used to distinguish target disease reports from taxonomy-only or near-neighbour mentions.

authoritative_evidence.name: ViralZone Ebolavirus Resource
authoritative_evidence.evidence_statement: ICTV separates orthoebolavirus species; Reston and Bombali viruses do not define the same human disease scope as Ebola virus disease.

authoritative_evidence.name: CDC Ebola Basics
